### Global Metadata
A complete 72-second original instrumental title-screen theme for a cozy Japanese slice-of-life game called Hare-machi Days, set in a sunny small town in early summer. Makoto Shinkai anime-film soundtrack feeling: nostalgic, hopeful, clear blue sky, warm light on stone streets. 72 BPM, D major, a simple memorable lyrical melody built on the IV-V-iii-vi royal-road progression. Intimate close-miked grand piano leads, supported by a soft warm string ensemble, a few celesta sparkles and a faint wind-chime shimmer. Gentle dynamics, natural room ambience, clean modern mix with delicate high-frequency detail. Pure instrumental chamber piece for piano, strings and celesta only. Avoid EDM drops, trap hi-hats, distorted guitars, heavy sub bass, trailer braams and cinematic bombast. No drum kit.

### Vocal Details
None. Instrumental only: the piano carries the melody; the strings answer with sustained harmony and a short counter-line.

### Timed Arrangement
0-12 seconds: solo piano states the main theme softly over broken-chord accompaniment. 12-32 seconds: warm strings enter underneath, the theme repeats with a celesta doubling an octave higher. 32-50 seconds: a gentle swell through the second phrase, strings take a brief counter-melody while the piano keeps flowing eighth notes. 50-64 seconds: settle back to piano and soft strings, end on a sustained D major chord with a natural decaying tail so the piece can loop back to its opening. The piece must play for the full 72 seconds and must not end early.
